title: MLC Super adds leadership roles targeting growth
full_text:
MLC Super has created two leadership roles covering its change program and employer superannuation business, appointing Lisa Croudace and Nerique Paterson as general managers.
Croudace joined the fund as general manager, portfolio delivery, on 14 September, while Paterson will join from Australian Retirement Trust in January 2027 as general manager, employer superannuation.
The appointments come as MLC Super undertakes a significant program of change while seeking to expand its presence in the employer market.
Paterson will oversee the fund’s employer growth and retention strategy, institutional partnerships, distribution channels and employer value proposition across corporate and small and medium enterprise segments.
She has spent the past eight years at Australian Retirement Trust, previously Sunsuper, most recently as general manager, commercial growth. Her experience includes growing the fund through corporate, institutional, SME and payroll ecosystem channels.
Before joining Sunsuper, Paterson was a senior consultant at Rice Warner.
MLC Super chief executive Dave Woodall said her experience would support the fund’s employer market ambitions.
“Nerique joins us with deep experience in employer superannuation, superannuation mergers and transitions, client retention, corporate growth and strategic partnerships.
“She has built her career helping superannuation funds grow through strong employer relationships and innovative growth initiatives, and will play an important role in strengthening our position in the employer market.”
Paterson said the opportunity to help shape the fund’s next phase of growth had attracted her to the position.
“The employer super market is evolving rapidly and there is a real opportunity to help more Australians engage with and get value from their superannuation,” she said.
“I’m looking forward to working with employers, partners and colleagues across the business to strengthen MLC Super’s employer value proposition in the market and build on the strong foundations already in place.”
Croudace’s responsibilities cover coordinating and executing the portfolio of change across MLC Super, with a focus on governance, prioritisation and delivery outcomes.
She brings more than two decades of experience across superannuation, wealth management and enterprise transformation, including senior leadership positions at Mercer Australia.
Her background also includes leading major transformation programs at BT Financial Group, including five successor fund transfers and the transfer of BT Super into Mercer Super.
“Lisa brings a proven track record in leading complex transformation in highly regulated environments, and her experience in transformation delivery, governance and strategic execution will help MLC Super maintain momentum across our delivery agenda and turn our priorities into meaningful outcomes for our members,” Woodall said.
Croudace said her role would focus on translating the fund’s priorities into delivery.
“My role is to help bring that vision to life through disciplined delivery, ensuring we focus on the initiatives that will have the greatest impact,” she said.
The appointments add to a leadership team that includes Amalie White, general manager, operations and partnerships; Craig Weber, head of education and advice; Jason Marler, general manager, master trust product; and Lachlan East, general manager, risk.
